lines.text: Thirty-three low atolls spread across the equator, settled by voyagers and now facing the rising sea. This is the story of Kiribati.
Micronesian voyagers settled these atolls thousands of years ago. In 1916, Britain made them part of the colony of the Gilbert and Ellice Islands.
In November 1943, American and Japanese forces fought for Tarawa atoll in one of the bloodiest battles of the Pacific war.
Ieremia Tabai, born in 1949, would become the first president of the new nation.
Anote Tong, born in 1952, would lead the country and warn the world that the rising sea threatens his people.
In 1957 and 1958, Britain tested hydrogen bombs at Malden and Kiritimati islands.
Taneti Maamau, born in 1960, would become president in 2016.
In 1979, the Gilberts became independent as Kiribati.
In 2008, Kiribati created the Phoenix Islands Protected Area, one of the largest marine reserves in the world.
Barely above the waves, Kiribati's story now turns on the rising sea.
